title: Pop a bridge stack and emit a symbol
statement: Let $c$ be a compiled program, let $x$ be a bridge input word, and choose optional bridge states $q,q'$, a valid input-head position $p$, an assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names, and an output word. If the stack at a chosen name $k$ is $a::xs$ and $e$ is an optional bridge-alphabet symbol, then applying the action that blanks the current cell of the work tape for $k$, moves that tape's head one cell to the right, and emits $e$, with successor state $q'$, gives the bridge configuration with state $q'$, the stack at $k$ replaced by $xs$, and output extended by $e$; the input-head position is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An assignment $st$ of stacks to the four stack names
A symbol $a$ and stack tail $xs$ with $st(k)=a::xs$
replaced:
Suppose that in a bridge configuration the stack at a name $k$ is nonempty, with top
symbol $a$ above a tail $xs$.  The one-tape pop action on the tape of $k$ (blank the
current cell, move right), extended with the emission of an optional output symbol
$e$, produces the bridge configuration whose stack at $k$ is $xs$ and whose output
is extended by $e$, the input position unchanged.
